title: Legislative districts of Maguindanao del Norte
wikitext:
{{Short description|Legislative district}} {{Politics of the Philippines}} The '''legislative district of Maguindanao del Norte''' were the representations of the [[Provinces of the Philippines|province]] of [[Maguindanao del Norte]] and the [[Cities of the Philippines#Independent cities|independent component city]] of [[Cotabato City|Cotabato]] in the [[List of legislatures of the Philippines|various national legislatures]] of the [[Philippines]]. The province and the city were represented in the [[House of Representatives of the Philippines|lower house]] of the [[Congress of the Philippines]] through their [[#Lone District|lone]] congressional district. == History == {{further|Legislative district of Mindanao and Sulu|Legislative district of Cotabato|Legislative districts of Maguindanao}} Before gaining separate representation, areas now under the jurisdiction of Maguindanao del Norte were represented under the [[Department of Mindanao and Sulu]] (1917–1935), [[Cotabato]] (1935–1972) and [[Maguindanao]] (1984–2007, 2010–2022). The enactment of Presidential Decree No. 341 on November 22, 1973, created the province of [[Maguindanao]] out of [[Cotabato]]'s [[Maguindanao people|Maguindanao-majority]] municipalities.{{cite web|title=Presidential Decree No. 341 - Creating the Provinces of North Cotabato, Maguindanao and Sultan Kudarat |url=http://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/1973/11/22/presidential-decree-no-341-s-1973/ |website=Official Gazette of the Republic of the Philippines |last=Marcos |first=Ferdinand E. |access-date=November 19, 2017 |date=November 22, 1973}} The new province was represented in the [[Interim Batasang Pambansa]] as part of [[Interim Batasang Pambansa#Regional Representatives|Region XII]] from 1978 to 1984. Maguindanao del Norte (including [[Cotabato City]]) first gained separate representation in [[1984 Philippine parliamentary election|1984]], when it returned [[#At-Large (defunct)|two representatives, elected at large]], to the [[Regular Batasang Pambansa]]. Under the new Constitution which was proclaimed on February 11, 1987, Maguindanao del Norte, including [[Cotabato City]], was retained into one congressional district;{{cite web|title=1987 Constitution of the Philippines - Apportionment Ordinance|website=Official Gazette of the Republic of the Philippines|url=http://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/the-1987-constitution-of-the-republic-of-the-philippines/the-1987-constitution-of-the-republic-of-the-philippines-ordinance/|author=1986 Constitutional Commission|date=February 2, 1987|access-date=November 19, 2017}} each elected its member to the restored [[House of Representatives of the Philippines|House of Representatives]] starting [[1987 Philippine legislative election|that same year]]. The province of [[Shariff Kabunsuan]], established with the passage of Muslim Mindanao Autonomy Act No. 201{{cite web|title=Muslim Mindanao Autonomy Act No. 201 - An Act Creating the Province of Shariff Kabunsuan, Providing Funds Therefor, and for Other Purposes|url=http://rla-armmgov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2015/03/MMAA-201.pdf|author=Regional Legislative Assembly - Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao|date=September 7, 2006|access-date=November 22, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170225122706/http://rla-armmgov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2015/03/MMAA-201.pdf|archive-date=February 25, 2017|url-status=dead}} and its subsequent [[2006 Shariff Kabunsuan creation plebiscite|approval by plebiscite]], was created out of Maguindanao's western municipalities in 2006. Per Section 5 of MMA Act No. 201, [[Cotabato City]] was grouped with Shariff Kabunsuan to elect a congressional representative. It was this specific provision that became the subject of the [[Sema v. COMELEC and Dilangalen|Supreme Court case]] that ultimately voided MMA Act No. 201 for being unconstitutional, and leading to the disestablishment of the Shariff Kabunsuan in 2008 and the return of its territory to [[Maguindanao]]. In the brief period of [[Shariff Kabunsuan]]'s existence, the [[#Lone District|First District of Maguindanao—Cotabato City]] was known as the ''Lone District of Shariff Kabunsuan—Cotabato City''. The enactment of Republic Act No. 11550 on May 28, 2021, separated the former province of Maguindanao into the provinces of Maguindanao del Norte and Maguindanao del Sur{{cite web|title=Republic Act No. 11550 - Charter of Maguindanao del Norte and Maguindanao del Sur|url=https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/downloads/2021/05may/20210527-RA-11550-RRD.pdf|author=Congress of the Philippines|date=May 28, 2021|access-date=May 28, 2021}} and its subsequent [[2022 Maguindanao division plebiscite|ratification by plebiscite]] on September 17, 2022, separated from Maguindanao's [[Legislative district of Maguindanao#1st District (defunct)|first district]] 1 city and 11 municipalities to create the province of [[Maguindanao del Norte]]. Per Section 9 of R.A. 11550, the new province was to comprise [[#Lone District|a single congressional district]]; voters began to elect the new province's separate representative beginning in [[2025 Philippine House of Representatives elections|2025]]. ==Lone District== {{See also|Maguindanao del Norte's at-large congressional district}} *'''[[Cities of the Philippines|City]]''': [[Cotabato City]] *'''[[Municipalities of the Philippines|Municipality]]''': [[Barira]], [[Buldon]], [[Datu Blah T.
